scripts.radio:
Hamjambo listeners, this is Kenya on Record. Today, we revisit the Hustler Fund promise that was supposed to lift small enterprises into sustainable growth.

When the fund launched, the headline pledge was straightforward: once personal micro-loans established borrowing histories, government would unveil the SME and chama facility. Small traders, mama mbogas, and artisans were promised enterprise credit of up to 2.5 million shillings at single-digit interest rates.

Four years in, where is that working capital? Our tracking shows the enterprise window remains effectively stalled. Millions of Kenyans continue to borrow and repay petty amounts—often between five hundred and two thousand shillings—yet the financing needed for serious restocking, commercial machinery, and premises expansion never arrived.

Meanwhile, informal traders remain at the mercy of predatory digital lenders and tough commercial bank terms. A national credit scheme that merely funds daily subsistence without building asset-owning enterprises cannot transform the economy. We must ask plainly: was this enterprise facility a genuine industrial policy, or simply political rhetoric to pacify small traders?

Kwa ufupi: Serikali iliahidi mikopo ya biashara ya hadi shilingi milioni mbili nukta tano kupitia Hustler Fund ili kukuza biashara ndogondogo. Hadi leo, mpango huo umekwama na wananchi wamebaki tu na mikopo midogo ya kibinafsi isiyoweza kukuza uchumi. Viongozi wanafaa kueleza fedha hizi zilikwama wapi.
scripts.voice_note: Habari zenu. Quick check-in from Kenya on Record on the Hustler Fund enterprise loans. Remember the big promise that chamas, small retailers, and jua kali groups would access up to 2.5 million shillings at low interest to expand their operations? Four years later, that enterprise window is virtually stalled. Most traders are still stuck recycling two thousand shillings on their phones, which cannot restock a kiosk, let alone buy equipment. Meanwhile, private credit is more expensive than ever. If billions were allocated to establish this fund, why hasn’t the SME facility reached the grassroots? We cannot keep celebrating emergency survival loans when real business capital was promised. Ask your area leaders where the enterprise fund went. Share this with your chama.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Ignore messages asking for upfront 'registration fees' to unlock Hustler Fund Sh2.5M enterprise loans. The SME rollout is stalled; fees are scams.
scripts.reels: Whatever happened to the 2.5-million-shilling Hustler Fund enterprise loans? Four years on, that small-business facility remains stalled. Millions of mama mbogas and small traders are still limited to tiny personal loans of two thousand shillings while waiting for real capital that never arrived. If public funds were set aside to expand your hustle, why is the SME window still shut? It’s Kenya on Record—let’s hold them to their word.
